papers.title: Model-Independent Determination of Intrinsic Leptonic CP Violation
papers.abstract:
Establishing leptonic Charge-Parity (CP) violation is a central goal of the next generation of long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. To achieve this, experimental analyses focus on excluding the CP-conserving values $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=0,\pi$ within the standard three-neutrino framework. We propose instead to establish CP violation as a phenomenon in a model-independent way. We use Gaussian Process regression to infer the $
u_\mu	o
u_e$ and $ ar
u_\mu	o ar
u_e$ appearance probabilities in a parametrization-free manner at DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande. By combining the two experiments, with mild assumptions on how matter impacts oscillations, we estimate how they can probe intrinsic CP violation in neutrino oscillations together. Taking the standard three-neutrino framework as a benchmark, we show that these experiments, when combined, can establish model-independent CP violation at $3\sigma$ for over 60% of the values of $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$.
papers.reason: Proposes a novel, parametrization-free approach using Gaussian Process regression to establish CP violation at DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande, directly aligning with the reader's core oscillation-analysis interests. [favorite author: Pedro Machado]

summary.tldr: DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande appearance data can establish leptonic CP violation model-independently at $3\sigma$ over 60% of $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$ values by isolating intrinsic vacuum asymmetry through Gaussian Process regression.
summary.novel_idea: Rather than testing $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \neq 0, \pi$ within the standard $3\nu$ oscillation model, the authors propose a parametrization-free determination of intrinsic leptonic CP violation. By using Gaussian Process (GP) regression directly on appearance probabilities as functions of $L/E$, and linearly combining DUNE and Hyper-K measurements weighted by their respective matter factors $\rho L$, the leading-order extrinsic matter asymmetry cancels completely, isolating the intrinsic CP-odd probability $P_{\rm CPV}$ without assuming a specific oscillation or matter-effect model.
summary.method: Mock event spectra at DUNE (624 kt-MW-yr) and Hyper-K (2431 kt-MW-yr) are generated based on NuFit 6.1 parameters with full detector smearing, efficiencies, and systematic uncertainties. Reconstructed appearance probabilities ($P_{\mu e}$ and $\bar{P}_{\mu e}$) are extracted using GP regression with a Matérn-5/2 kernel marginalized over hyperparameters. Hypothesis testing between the data-conditioned GP and a CP-conserving null prior ($P_{\rm CPV} = 0$) is performed using a marginal-likelihood evidence-ratio test statistic calibrated with data-driven pseudo-experiments.
key_results: Identifies model-independent intrinsic leptonic CP violation at $\ge 3\sigma$ CL for over 60% of true $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$ values, and $\ge 5\sigma$ CL for ~30% of the parameter space.

DUNE provides $\langle N_{\mathrm{eff}} \rangle \approx 12$ functional degrees of freedom and $\langle I \rangle \approx 20$ nats of mutual information, whereas Hyper-K provides $\langle N_{\mathrm{eff}} \rangle \approx 7$ and $\langle I \rangle \approx 12$ nats due to its narrower energy band.
Demonstrates that the linear expansion in $\rho L$ reproduces the true vacuum asymmetry to high accuracy while retaining sensitivity to intrinsic new-physics CP violation such as sterile neutrinos.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts long-baseline oscillation phenomenology (DUNE and Hyper-K) by providing an analysis framework that is robust against BSM matter effects or non-unitarity. It also showcases an advanced application of Gaussian Processes for unfolding detector and interaction model effects into model-independent oscillation probabilities.
summary.caveats: Relies on the leading-order expansion in $\rho L$ to cancel matter effects, assuming average Earth matter densities that carry an assumed 3% systematic uncertainty, and requires data from both DUNE and Hyper-K.

papers.title: A High-Energy Neutrino Collider within a Muon Collider
papers.reason: Examines high-energy neutrino-lepton scattering and electroweak dynamics at a multi-TeV muon collider using EFT, squarely hitting the reader's core BSM and neutrino interaction interests. [favorite author: Andre de Gouvea]

summary.tldr: Electroweak collinear $W^\pm$ emissions turn a 10 TeV muon collider into a high-energy neutrino collider, probing four-lepton SMEFT operators up to 250 TeV and lifting flat directions.
summary.novel_idea:
The paper demonstrates that electroweak gauge-boson radiation off multi-TeV muon beams generates substantial $\mu
u_\mu$ and $
u_\mu ar{
u}_\mu$ partonic luminosities, effectively embedding a high-energy neutrino-lepton collider within a muon collider. Supplementing dominant charged-current/neutral-current $\mu^+\mu^-$ collisions with neutrino-initiated partonic channels utilizes $SU(2)_L$ gauge symmetry to lift degeneracies among Wilson coefficients in global SMEFT fits that cannot be broken by charged-lepton collisions alone.
summary.method:
The authors employ electroweak parton distribution functions (EW PDFs) for leptons and neutrinos within a collinear factorization framework at a $\sqrt{s}=10$ TeV muon collider ($10	ext{ ab}^{-1}$). They evaluate four-lepton dimension-6 operators in the Warsaw basis for processes $\mu^+\mu^- 	o \ell^+\ell^-$, $
u_\mu\mu^\pm 	o 
u_\ell\ell'^\pm$, and $
u_\mu ar{
u}_\mu 	o \ell^+\ell^-$, comparing single- and multi-operator sensitivities to low-energy electroweak and LFV precision bounds. They also map the results to resonant and virtual exchanges in sequential $W'$ and $Z'$ models via the radiative return mechanism.
key_results: Single-operator SMEFT reach for flavor-conserving and flavor-violating four-lepton operators reaches effective scales $\Lambda \sim 75 - 250$ TeV (Wilson coefficients $10^{-5} - 10^{-4}\text{ TeV}^{-2}$), surpassing LEP-2 and low-energy bounds.

Including $\mu\nu_\mu$-initiated channels directly breaks flat directions between pairs of Wilson coefficients such as $(C_{1122}^{\ell\ell}, C_{2211}^{\ell e})$ and $(C_{2222}^{\ell\ell}, C_{2222}^{\ell e})$.

Resonant radiative return at $\sqrt{s} = 10$ TeV probes sequential $W'$ couplings down to $\zeta_{\rm SSM} \sim 10^{-3}$ up to $M_{W'} \approx 10$ TeV, and smoothly connects to four-lepton contact operators for $M_{W'} \gg 10$ TeV.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to high-energy neutrino interactions, electroweak PDF development, and SMEFT matching/running in lepton-collider environments. It demonstrates how high-energy neutrino scattering channels can directly resolve BSM operator degeneracies at future facilities.
summary.caveats: Analysis is conducted primarily at leading order in the EW PDF formalism; full detector simulations, beam-induced backgrounds, and forward muon/neutrino tagging efficiencies were not modeled.

papers.title: Neutrino electromagnetic properties after the first $pp$ solar neutrino observation at XENONnT
papers.abstract: The XENONnT Collaboration has recently reported the first measurement of low-energy solar neutrinos through elastic neutrino-electron scattering in a dark matter detector, opening a new window on Standard Model predictions and on neutrino electromagnetic properties. We analyze these data to extract the $pp$ neutrino flux normalization and the weak mixing angle at low momentum transfer ($\sim 0.1$ MeV). We also derive bounds on the neutrino charge radii, magnetic moments, and millicharges, as well as on the sterile-neutrino dipole portal. Since the $pp$-flux determination displays a mild excess, we further investigate the role of the $^{14}$C background in the fit and assess how it affects the extracted parameters. Our results show that dark matter detectors now offer a probe of neutrino physics that is complementary to dedicated precision experiments.
papers.reason: Analyzes XENONnT low-energy solar neutrino data to constrain neutrino electromagnetic properties (charge radii, magnetic moments, millicharges) and Weinberg angle, squarely in the core low-energy neutrino physics interest. [favorite author: Dimitrios Papoulias]

summary.tldr: XENONnT's first detection of $pp$ solar neutrinos via electron scattering constrains neutrino charge radii, millicharges, magnetic moments, and sterile dipole portals while probing low-$|q|$ $\sin^2\theta_W$.
summary.novel_idea: This is the first phenomenological exploitation of the real-time $pp$ solar neutrino electron-recoil detection reported by XENONnT (1 keV threshold) to constrain neutrino electromagnetic properties and electroweak parameters at momentum transfers $|q| \sim 0.1$ MeV. The study specifically quantifies how a potential unmodeled $^{14}$C background influences the observed $\sim 2\sigma$ excess in the extracted $pp$ flux and shifts the inferred BSM limits.
summary.method:
The authors analyze XENONnT science runs (SR0 and SR1b) in the 1–140 keV electron recoil range using the MB22m standard solar model flux and full 3-flavor MSW oscillation probabilities. They perform $\chi^2$ profile analyses with atomic binding corrections ($Z_{m eff}(T_e)$) to extract the $pp$ flux normalization, $\sin^2	heta_W$, flavor-dependent neutrino charge radii $\langle r_
u^2 angle$, millicharges $q_
u$, effective magnetic moments $\mu_
u$, and the active-to-sterile dipole upscattering portal $
u_\ell + e^- 	o 
u_4 + e^-$, both with and without floating a $^{14}$C background component.
key_results: Extracted $pp$ flux without $^{14}$C is $\Phi_{pp} = (10.74^{+2.26}_{-2.25}) \times 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$ ($2.1\sigma$ above MB22m); including $^{14}$C reduces it to $(9.03^{+2.76}_{-2.41}) \times 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$ ($1.3\sigma$ tension).
The weak mixing angle at $|q| \sim 0.1$ MeV is extracted as $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.465^{+0.075}_{-0.087}$ (without $^{14}$C) and $0.407^{+0.099}_{-0.115}$ (with $^{14}$C).

Obtains 90% CL bounds: effective magnetic moment $\mu_\nu^{\rm eff} < 1.35 \times 10^{-11}\mu_B$ (with $^{14}$C), millicharges $|q_{\nu_{ee}}| \lesssim 1.8 \times 10^{-12}e$, and charge radii $\mathcal{O}(10^{-30}\text{ cm}^2)$.
Sterile dipole portal bounds reach $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 2 \times 10^{-11}\mu_B$ for $m_4 \lesssim 100$ keV, extending to $m_4 \approx 560$ keV before hitting the $^7$Be kinematic cutoff.
summary.why_it_matters: Connects low-energy solar neutrino flux measurements to precision electroweak tests and light BSM portals (dipole portal, millicharges). It also highlights the critical role of low-energy background modeling ($^{14}$C) for interpreting sub-10 keV electron recoils in noble liquid detectors.
summary.caveats: The current dataset displays a $\sim 2\sigma$ excess over the standard solar model which biases the unconstrained fits toward non-zero magnetic moments/millicharges unless the $^{14}$C nuisance parameter is fully unconstrained.

papers.title: Measurements of transverse kinematic imbalance in muon neutrino charged-current interactions on argon with a single proton and no pions in the final state with SBND
papers.abstract: This letter presents the first neutrino-argon cross-section measurement from the Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory. We report the nominal flux-averaged single-differential cross sections of muon neutrino charged-current interactions on argon with a single proton and no pions in the final state as functions of the transverse kinematic imbalance variables. Using a subset of Run~1 data corresponding to $8.8\times10^{19}$ protons-on-target, we select 12,804 signal candidates with a purity of 91%. The extracted cross sections discriminate strongly among event-generator predictions, owing to the high statistics and the design of the analysis. Among the compared models, none successfully describes all three variables, with the largest discrepancies in the transverse missing momentum variable. These results set new benchmarks for neutrino-argon interaction modeling, which is crucial for high-precision measurements at current and future accelerator neutrino experiments.
authors: G. A. N. Buzzard (The SBND Collaboration)
V. do Lago Pimentel (The SBND Collaboration)
V. C. L. Nguyen (The SBND Collaboration)
O. L. G. Peres (The SBND Collaboration)
R. Van de Water (The SBND Collaboration)
papers.reason: Presents the first SBND cross-section measurement of muon neutrino interactions on argon with a single proton and no pions using transverse kinematic imbalance, directly in the reader's core experimental and theoretical interest.

summary.tldr: SBND reports its first $\nu_\mu\text{CC}1p0\pi$ cross sections on argon versus transverse kinematic imbalance variables, showing strong model discrimination and significant discrepancies in transverse missing momentum.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first physics cross-section results from the SBND LArTPC at Fermilab, utilizing 12,804 candidate $\nu_\mu\text{CC}1p0\pi$ events with 91% purity. It provides high-statistics single-differential cross sections in the transverse kinematic imbalance (TKI) variables ($\delta p_T$, $\delta\alpha_T$, $\delta\phi_T$) on argon, providing an unprecedentedly sharp benchmark that isolates nuclear Fermi motion and final-state interactions (FSI) from neutrino flux normalization.
summary.method:
Using $8.8\times 10^{19}$ POT from the BNB ($
avg{E_\nu} = 0.75$ GeV) in Run 1, events are reconstructed using Pandora pattern recognition within LArSoft, requiring fully contained two-track events with $p_\mu \in [0.22, 1.0]$ GeV/$c$ and $p_p \in [0.3, 1.0]$ GeV/$c$. Unfolding is performed via Wiener-SVD with second-derivative regularization smearing matrices $A_C$. The extracted differential cross sections are compared via NUISANCE to GENIE v3.4.0 (including empirical, Local Fermi Gas, Spectral Function, and Hartree-Fock nuclear models), NEUT v6.1.4, and GiBUU 2025.
key_results: 12,804 signal events selected with 91% purity (80% genuine CCQE according to GENIE).
None of the generators (GENIE AR23, GiBUU 2025, NEUT v6.1.4) successfully describes all three TKI variables simultaneously.

The largest tension appears in the transverse missing momentum $\delta p_T$: GENIE AR23 underpredicts the peak and intermediate region ($0.1 < \delta p_T < 0.4$ GeV/$c$) and overpredicts the tail ($\delta p_T > 0.4$ GeV/$c$).

Hartree-Fock nuclear ground-state implementations improve the $\delta p_T$ peak description but degrade the slope in $\delta\alpha_T$, whereas GiBUU predicts a significantly steeper $\delta\alpha_T$ slope than observed.
summary.why_it_matters: Core research topic. This is a critical benchmark for neutrino-argon interaction modeling directly impacting DUNE and SBN oscillation analyses. It tests whether nuclear ground states (Hartree-Fock vs. Spectral Function vs. Fermi Gas) and FSI cascades in GENIE, GiBUU, and NEUT can reproduce exclusive semi-inclusive topology kinematics.
summary.caveats: Cross sections are single-differential and flux-averaged over the broad BNB spectrum; full multi-differential correlations ($(\delta p_T, \delta\alpha_T)$) will require larger POT statistics. Secondary interaction reweighting uncertainties in Geant4 remain sizable for low-energy protons.

papers.title: Muon-to-positron conversion from light Majorana neutrino exchange: nuclear responses and pion-pole-improved multipoles
papers.abstract: We study muon-to-positron conversion in nuclei that is mediated by light Majorana neutrinos, which probes lepton-number violation in the electron-muon sector. As the second paper in a series, this work extends our study of local dimension-nine interactions to the mass mechanism. We derive the conversion amplitude from the second-order effective four-Fermi interaction and express it in terms of nuclear responses in the one-body impulse approximation. Using phenomenological nucleon form factors, we retain convection, axial charge, weak magnetism, and the longitudinal pion-pole current in a specified pion-pole-improved prescription. The two physical time orderings and the distinct momentum transfers are derived in the intermediate-state response. We complete its angular reduction and derive the corresponding closure operator, including spin-gradient terms. Both the symmetric (scalar) and antisymmetric (vector) lepton-hadron Lorentz contractions contribute to the spin-averaged, angle-integrated rate. For $0^+\!\to0^+$ transitions we give explicit formulas in terms of two coherent radial amplitudes, without restricting the intermediate nuclei to spin zero. This provides an interface to nuclear calculations of the required nuclear matrix elements. However, in this work, no isotope-specific numerical predictions are attempted. The present treatment uses approximate lepton wavefunctions and recoil-free nuclear propagation. Two-body weak currents and systematic chiral effective-field-theory matching are left for future work.
papers.reason: Derives nuclear responses and pion-pole-improved multipoles for muon-to-positron conversion mediated by light Majorana neutrinos, hitting core interests in lepton-number violation and nuclear electroweak processes.

summary.tldr: The nuclear response and closure formalism for light Majorana neutrino-mediated $\mu^- \to e^+$ conversion is derived using pion-pole-improved nucleon currents and effective momentum Coulomb corrections.
summary.novel_idea: The paper provides the first systematic derivation of the nuclear matrix element framework for light Majorana neutrino-mediated nuclear $\mu^- \to e^+$ conversion starting from second-order weak interactions with a pion-pole-improved (PI) one-body nucleon current. Unlike neutrinoless double-beta decay, the conversion features large momentum transfers, non-degenerate time orderings with physical on-shell intermediate states, and non-vanishing coherent contributions from both symmetric (scalar) and antisymmetric (vector) lepton-hadron tensor contractions even for $0^+ \to 0^+$ nuclear transitions.
summary.method: The second-order $S$-matrix element is derived in the one-body impulse approximation retaining convection, axial charge, weak magnetism, and the longitudinal pseudoscalar pion pole. The authors perform a complete spherical harmonic angular reduction of the intermediate-state resolvent (spectral formulation) and also construct the closure approximation including spin-gradient two-body operators. Lepton wavefunctions are incorporated using an initial-state bound $1s$ muon density-average and the Effective Momentum Approximation (EMA) for the Coulomb-distorted outgoing relativistic positron.
key_results: Explicitly shows that $0^+ \to 0^+$ transitions depend coherently on two complex radial amplitudes, $\mathcal{A}_0(P)$ (scalar) and $\mathcal{B}_0(P)$ (vector), proving that the antisymmetric hadron tensor does not vanish for spin-zero endpoints due to the directional vector supplied by the positron momentum.

Establishes the intermediate resolvent denominators with absorptive on-shell parts: $\omega_\ell - (m_\mu - E_b - \Delta_n) - i\epsilon$ (muon-first) and $\omega_\ell + E_e + \Delta_n - i\epsilon$ (positron-first).

Provides a ready-to-use operator inventory and radial kernel formulas classification for nuclear many-body calculations targeting experimental isotopes ($^{48}\text{Ti} \to {}^{48}\text{Ca}$, $^{27}\text{Al} \to {}^{27}\text{Na}$, $^{32}\text{S}$, $^{40}\text{Ca}$).
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts theoretical modeling of lepton number violation in the muon-electron sector probed by Mu2e, COMET, and Mu2e-II. The treatment of nucleon form factors, pion-pole currents, and closure vs. intermediate-state responses closely parallels nuclear EFT and electroweak response calculations in neutrino physics.
summary.caveats: No isotope-specific numerical calculations of nuclear matrix elements are carried out in this work; two-body meson-exchange currents and systematic chiral EFT power-counting matching are deferred to future papers.

papers.title: Absorption of bound supernova axion-like particles by the neutron star weakens the heating limits on their photon coupling
papers.abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) that couple to protons are produced in a core-collapse supernova, and the slow ones remain bound to the new neutron star. Bose, Ganguly, Kumar, and Raj [arXiv:2610.30255] proposed that the photons from the decay of this bound cloud reheat old neutron stars, and they derived strong limits on the ALP-photon coupling. They neglected the absorption of the ALPs by the star, but a bound ALP on an orbit that enters the star and reaches 50 km crosses it about $6\times 10^{18}$ times over the 333 Myr age of PSR J2144$-$3933. We show that inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung in the cold star absorbs every ALP whose orbit enters it within minutes, long before it decays, so only ALPs born outside the final star on nearly circular orbits survive; they carry $9\times 10^{-9} - 6\times 10^{-5}$ of the heating. We compute the protoneutron-star evolution, the production, the general-relativistic orbits and the absorption ourselves, for twelve protoneutron-star evolutions, three nucleon-bremsstrahlung rates normalized to the same supernova energy loss of light ALPs, and equations of state with and without $\Delta(1232)$ isobars. PSR J2144$-$3933 still excludes a window at $m_a\simeq 7.7-196$\ MeV, with a lower edge in the photon coupling $280-700$ times higher than without absorption. Pion conversion and the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which raise the production of surviving ALPs more than their absorption, widen this window to $m_a\simeq$ $7.7-260$\ MeV. The window depends at similar levels on the bremsstrahlung rate and on the radius of the final star. It requires a direct photon coupling that cancels the one induced by ALP-pion mixing, and existing supernova gamma-ray limits may already cover it.
papers.reason: Demonstrates that inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung in neutron stars absorbs bound supernova ALPs and reevaluates photon-coupling heating limits, sitting precisely at the intersection of supernova neutrinos, dark sectors, and nuclear astrophysics.

summary.tldr: Inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung absorbs bound supernova ALPs orbiting through the neutron star within minutes, weakening old neutron star heating limits on $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$ by several orders of magnitude.
summary.novel_idea: The paper demonstrates that axion-like particles (ALPs) bound in the gravitational basin of a supernova remnant pass through the neutron star $\sim 10^{18}$ times over stellar lifetimes and are rapidly re-absorbed via inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung. This invalidates previous assumptions of free streaming for bound populations. Consequently, only particles on non-star-crossing, nearly circular orbits born outside the final radius survive to contribute to late-time stellar reheating.
summary.method: The authors perform general-relativistic orbit integrations using adiabatic invariants ($L$ and radial action $J_r$) across 12 protoneutron star (PNS) cooling simulations and 19 cold neutron star relativistic mean-field equations of state (including $\Delta(1232)$ resonances). They compute ALP absorption and emission via one-pion exchange, $\rho$ exchange, and pion conversion ($a n \to \pi^- p$). The surviving decay photon luminosity is compared against the HST thermal upper bound for PSR J2144$-$3933.
key_results: Bound ALPs on star-crossing orbits are absorbed via inverse bremsstrahlung within $0.1\text{ s}$ to $7\text{ min}$, reducing the surviving heating fraction to $9\times 10^{-9} - 6\times 10^{-5}$ of the unabsorbed expectation.

Exclusion limits on $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$ from PSR J2144$-$3933 are weakened by factors of $280-700$, leaving an open sensitivity window at $m_a \simeq 7.7-196\text{ MeV}$ ($7.7-260\text{ MeV}$ when including $\pi^-$ conversion and $\Delta$ resonances).

The $np$ bremsstrahlung channel significantly accelerates cold-star absorption (by factors of $17-80$ at $100-200\text{ MeV}$), and the surviving heating margin varies by a factor of $\sim 5$ between stellar radii $R = 11.5\text{ km}$ and $13.5\text{ km}$.
summary.why_it_matters: The analysis connects dense-matter nuclear equations of state, in-medium nucleon-nucleon bremsstrahlung, and protoneutron star evolution to BSM particle emission from core-collapse supernovae.
summary.caveats: The surviving ALP parameter window requires an accidental cancellation between the bare photon coupling and the pion-mixing-induced coupling to one part in $10^4-10^5$, and may already be excluded by un-recast supernova gamma-ray limits.

papers.title: Predicting $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ states from a reanalysis of lattice QCD data
papers.abstract: We reanalyze the lattice QCD data for the isoscalar $\bar b\bar c ud$ systems with $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ at $m_{\pi}\simeq 220$ MeV, incorporating both short- and long-range interactions constrained by heavy-quark spin and chiral symmetries. Using the interaction fitted to the lattice results, we predict a spectrum of isoscalar $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ molecular states with quantum numbers $J^P=0^+$, $1^+$, and $2^+$. The predicted $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $B\bar D$ and $B^*\bar D$ bound states are consistent with the lattice results. Furthermore, the two resonances reported by the lattice collaboration in the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $\bar b\bar c ud$ channels can be naturally interpreted as $B^*\bar D{}^*$ and $B\bar D{}^*$ hadronic molecules, respectively. We also predict two previously unreported $B^*\bar D{}^*$ states with $J^P=1^+$ and $2^+$: a bound state and a shallow state whose pole may correspond to either a virtual state or a bound state, respectively. Our results provide a unified interpretation of the lattice spectrum and highlight the interplay between short- and long-range interactions in the dynamics of the $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ systems.
papers.reason: Reanalyzes lattice QCD data to predict open-flavor heavy molecular states using heavy-quark spin and chiral symmetries, intersecting with ab initio and hadronic interactions. [favorite author: Juan Nieves]

summary.tldr: Reanalyzing lattice QCD data for isoscalar $\bar{b}\bar{c}ud$ systems using heavy-quark spin and chiral effective field theory predicts a spectrum of bound and resonant molecular $B^{(*)}\bar{D}^{(*)}$ states across $J^P=0^+, 1^+, 2^+$.
summary.novel_idea: The authors project chiral effective field theory potentials (contact plus one-pion exchange) onto cubic group representations ($A_1^+, T_1^+$) to perform a consistent finite-volume reanalysis of HAL QCD / lattice energy levels. By utilizing heavy-quark spin symmetry (HQSS), they correlate disparate spin-parity channels to predict both observed and missing molecular tetraquark states.
summary.method: The framework solves the Lippmann-Schwinger equation in both infinite and finite volume with Gaussian cutoff regularization ($\Lambda = 0.8, 1.2\text{ GeV}$). Low-energy constants are fitted to the lowest lattice energy levels of $J^P=0^+$ ($B\bar{D}$) and $J^P=1^+$ ($B^*\bar{D}$ - $B\bar{D}^*$), and the resulting amplitudes are analytically continued to find pole positions on unphysical Riemann sheets.
key_results: Confirms shallow $B\bar{D}$ ($J^P=0^+$) and $B^*\bar{D}$ ($J^P=1^+$) bound states with binding energies of a few MeV ($1-3\text{ MeV}$ and $2-6\text{ MeV}$, respectively).

Interprets higher resonances reported on the lattice as predominantly molecular states: a $J^P=0^+$ $B^*\bar{D}^*$ state bound by $15-41\text{ MeV}$ and a $J^P=1^+$ $B\bar{D}^*$ state bound by $1-14\text{ MeV}$.
Predicts two previously unobserved isoscalar $B^*\bar{D}^*$ states: a $J^P=1^+$ bound state (binding energy $1-7\text{ MeV}$) and a shallow $J^P=2^+$ state (bound or virtual).
summary.why_it_matters: While co-authored by Juan Nieves, this work focuses strictly on exotic heavy-meson spectroscopy and hadron molecules rather than electroweak or neutrino interactions.
summary.caveats: Coupled-channel interactions to higher vector-vector channels ($B^*\bar{D}^*$) are neglected due to the lack of nonlocal two-meson operators in current lattice data.

papers.title: Nuclei on the Light Front and Electron Scattering
papers.abstract: This paper develops relativistic nuclear structure, motivated by past, current and future experi- ments at Jefferson Lab and the Electron-Ion Collider. Building on existing tools from conventional nuclear physics, we reformulate them in a relativistic, light-front-quantized framework. Our light- front nuclear structure calculations reproduce nuclear binding energies and shell structure well, and incorporate the physics of nucleon-nucleon short-ranged-correlations (SRCs) through similarity renormalization group techniques. Our results are that a purely nucleonic description is insufficient to capture inclusive electron-nucleus scattering data. It does not fully reproduce the plateaus seen at high Bjorken-xB, pointing to the importance of non-nucleonic dynamics responsible for the EMC effect
papers.reason: Develops a relativistic light-front framework for nuclear structure, short-range correlations, and inclusive electron-nucleus scattering, closely matching the reader's interest in electron scattering constraints.

summary.tldr: Develops a relativistic light-front nuclear structure framework incorporating mean-field theory and similarity-renormalization-group short-range correlations, showing purely nucleonic models fail to explain inclusive electron-nucleus scattering plateaus at $x_B > 1.5$.
summary.novel_idea: The paper maps instant-form relativistic mean-field theory wavefunctions exactly to the boost-invariant light front, then incorporates nucleon-nucleon short-range correlations (SRCs) and $2N + (A-2)$ final-state continuum configurations using light-front Similarity Renormalization Group (SRG) unitary transformations.
summary.method: The authors solve light-front quasi-elastic kinematics in collinear frames for inclusive $A(e,e')$ scattering. Initial bound states are constructed from light-front mean-field theory (Horowitz-Serot type). High-momentum components are generated by evolving the Argonne $v_{18}$ (AV18) potential with SRG flow equations. Final-state interactions (FSI) between the correlated pair are incorporated via the half-off-shell two-nucleon $T$-matrix.
key_results: Light-front relativistic mean-field theory reproduces the quasi-elastic peak ($0.8 < x_B < 1.3$) on $^{16}\text{O}$ and $^{40}\text{Ca}$ from JLab data, but severely underestimates cross sections at $x_B > 1.3$.

SRG-induced two-nucleon SRC configurations supply high-momentum tails, while elastic two-nucleon FSI corrections are shown to be small (interference and quadratic terms are $1-2$ orders of magnitude below the cross section).

While nucleonic SRCs describe deuterium data well up to $x_B \approx 1.8$, they significantly underestimate heavy-nucleus ($^{40}\text{Ca}$) data, demonstrating that experimental $a_2(A)$ cross-section ratio plateaus are driven by non-nucleonic inelastic processes (such as $\Delta$ or meson production allowed at high $x_B$ on nuclear targets) rather than purely nucleonic SRC abundance.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts the theoretical foundation of electron-nucleus and neutrino-nucleus event generators (e4nu, GENIE, Achilles). It provides a frame-independent, relativistic treatment of initial nuclear states and demonstrates that 2p2h/SRC models cannot neglect relativistic kinematics and inelastic non-nucleonic channels when interpreting high-momentum transfer data.
summary.caveats: Uses an approximate 'minimal-relativity' transformed AV18 potential instead of a genuinely light-front chiral NN potential, and does not yet include explicit isobar or quark degrees of freedom in the final state.

papers.title: Gluon gravitational form factors of the proton from near-threshold charmonium photoproduction
papers.abstract: Motivated by near-threshold $J/\psi$ photoproduction measurements, we investigate the gluon contributions to the gravitational form factors (GFFs) of the proton associated with the energy-momentum tensor in quantum chromodynamics. We calculate the gluon GFFs and the corresponding mechanical properties of the proton within a light-front spectator model, in which the proton is described as an active gluon accompanied by a spectator particle. The model parameters are determined from a global fit to the differential cross section for $J/\psi$ photoproduction. The resulting gluon GFFs are in reasonable agreement with recent lattice QCD determinations. We further calculate the total cross section and find reasonable agreement with the available experimental data. Using the extracted gluon GFFs, we investigate the two-dimensional light-front gluon distributions inside the proton, such as the mass, angular momentum, pressure, and shear force distributions. We also study the gluonic contributions to the two-dimensional Galilean energy density, radial and tangential pressures, isotropic pressure, and pressure anisotropy.
papers.reason: Extracts gluon gravitational form factors of the proton from near-threshold charmonium photoproduction using a light-front spectator model, highly relevant to nucleon structure and generalized parton distributions.

summary.tldr: Evaluates proton gluon gravitational form factors and 2D mechanical pressure distributions using a light-front spectator model fitted to near-threshold $J/\psi$ photoproduction cross-section data from Jefferson Lab.
summary.novel_idea: Calculates all four gluon gravitational form factors ($A_g, B_g, D_g, \bar{C}_g$) simultaneously from light-front wavefunctions in a spectator framework, deriving 2D transverse mechanical profiles (radial and tangential pressures, shear force, Galilean energy densities) directly from heavy quarkonium photoproduction data.
summary.method: The proton is modeled as an active gluon plus a three-quark spectator with Brodsky-Hwang-Lepage vertex regularization. Free parameters are constrained by a global fit to differential cross sections of $\gamma p \to J/\psi p$ from GlueX and $J/\psi$-007 at JLab within a leading-order non-relativistic QCD and second-Mellin-moment GPD framework.
key_results: Extracted gluon gravitational form factors $A_g(t)$, $B_g(t)$, and $D_g(t)$ show good qualitative agreement with unquenched lattice QCD determinations at $\mu = 2\text{ GeV}$.
Determines the off-forward EMT non-conservation parameter at the origin to be $\bar{C}_g(0) = -0.050 \pm 0.009$, matching the negative sign predicted in instanton vacuum models.

Confirms 2D mechanical stability criteria (von Laue condition $\int d^2r_\perp \mathcal{P}_g(r_\perp) = 0$), yielding a core mass density of $\mathcal{E}_g(0) = 2.45 \pm 0.68\text{ GeV/fm}^2$ and positive radial pressure across the entire proton transverse radius.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a relativistic light-front perspective on hadron structure, but focuses on gluonic energy-momentum tensor distributions rather than electroweak (axial/vector) form factors relevant to neutrino scattering.
summary.caveats: The extracted $D_g(t)$ exhibits an unphysical logarithmic divergence as $t \to 0$, preventing a clean determination of the gluonic mechanical radius; the model also omits higher-spin spectators.

papers.title: Searching for Dark Photons and ALPs using Gamma-rays from Nuclear Reactors
papers.abstract: Nuclear reactors are intense sources of MeV gamma rays, produced in fission, radiative neutron capture and the de-excitation of fission products. Building on earlier phenomenological studies, we present a detector-independent description of the production of light, weakly coupled particles by reactor gamma rays and of their detection through scattering, absorption and decay in a nearby detector. We consider kinetically mixed dark photons, produced and detected through Compton-like processes, and axion-like particles (ALPs) coupled to photons, electrons and nucleons, produced through Primakoff conversion, Compton-like scattering and magnetic nuclear transitions such as the $2.23~\mathrm{MeV}$ line of $p(n,\gamma)d$. As a concrete application, we derive the projected sensitivities of the CONUS+ germanium experiment at the Leibstadt reactor and of a conceivable $100$-kg CONUS100 upgrade. For sub-MeV dark photons, CONUS+ and CONUS100 reach kinetic mixings of $\epsilon\simeq1.65\times10^{-5}$ and $1.2\times10^{-5}$, respectively, for $0.5~\mathrm{keV}\lesssim m_{A'}\lesssim0.5~\mathrm{MeV}$. For ALPs, we show that CONUS100 can probe an unexplored region of parameter space at MeV masses, in particular through $a\to e^+e^-$ decays of ALPs emitted in the deuteron line, assuming a energy window extended to $10~\mathrm{MeV}$.
papers.topic: Dark Photons and ALPs from Reactors
papers.reason: Derives sensitivities of reactor neutrino/gamma experiments (CONUS+) to dark photons and axion-like particles via nuclear gamma transitions, directly matching the reader's core interest in reactor and low-energy BSM searches.

summary.tldr: Derives reactor gamma-ray production and detection rates for dark photons and ALPs, demonstrating that the CONUS+ and CONUS100 CEvNS germanium detectors can probe new sub-MeV dark photon and MeV-scale ALP parameter space.
summary.novel_idea: Constructs an updated detector-independent framework for MeV-scale light weakly coupled particle production in nuclear reactor cores—incorporating full finite-mass kinematics, uranium photoelectric absorption corrections, and monochromatic magnetic transitions ($M1, M4$) alongside continuous fission spectra—and applies it to Germanium CEvNS experiments.
summary.method: The authors model continuous gamma spectra from the $3.6\text{ GW}$ Leibstadt reactor core and discrete gamma lines (notably the $2.23\text{ MeV}$ line from $p(n,\gamma)d$). They compute Compton-like production/detection for dark photons and Primakoff, Compton-like, axio-electric, and $a \to e^+e^-$ channels for ALPs, projecting sensitivities for the CONUS+ setup (4 kg HPGe, $20.7\text{ m}$ baseline) and a 100-kg CONUS100 upgrade under a flat 10 DRU background benchmark.
key_results: For sub-MeV kinetically mixed dark photons, CONUS+ and CONUS100 achieve sensitivities of $\epsilon \simeq 1.65\times 10^{-5}$ and $1.2\times 10^{-5}$ respectively for $0.5\text{ keV} \lesssim m_{A'} \lesssim 0.5\text{ MeV}$, improving upon reanalyzed TEXONO limits by factors of $1.6-2.2$.

Single-coupling ALP limits for $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$ and $g_{aee}$ lie within regions already constrained by solar/terrestrial experiments, but CONUS100 can access previously unconstrained territory for MeV-scale ALPs via $a \to e^+e^-$ from the $2.23\text{ MeV}$ deuteron line, reaching $|g_{aee} g_{ann}^{(1)}| \simeq 1.3\times 10^{-15}$.

Demonstrates that an extended DAQ readout window (up to $10\text{ MeV}$, compared to the current $0.6\text{ MeV}$ threshold) is essential for reactor CEvNS experiments to probe new MeV-scale BSM parameter space.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly touches low-energy reactor experiments used for coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS). It highlights how low-threshold HPGe detector technology can be repurposed to search for light BSM mediators and ALPs.
summary.caveats: Relies on a flat background benchmark of 10 DRU without modeling detector containment, escape of annihilation photons, or pulse-shape discrimination efficiencies; uncovering new ALP parameter space strictly requires widening the detector DAQ energy window.

papers.title: Ab Initio Calculations of $^6$He + $p$ Reactions
papers.abstract: The no-core shell model with continuum (NCSMC) is an ab initio framework for description of nuclear structure and reactions. Recent developments of the NCSMC allow for calculations of charge-exchange and nucleon-transfer reactions. We have applied the NCSMC to calculate cross sections of the ($p,p$), ($p,n$), and ($p,t$) reactions on radioactive $^6$He, using chiral nuclear forces as input.
papers.reason: Applies the ab initio NCSMC framework with chiral nuclear forces to calculate charge-exchange and nucleon-transfer reactions on radioactive He-6, directly matching core ab initio electroweak responses and reaction calculations.

papers.title: Configuration-Interaction Studies of Alpha Clustering in Atomic Nuclei
papers.abstract: Clustering in atomic nuclei, and $\alpha$ clustering in particular, is a striking form of self-organization in quantum many-body systems, emerging from nucleon--nucleon interactions through the interplay of correlations, symmetry constraints, and continuum coupling. We summarize a configuration-interaction approach in which cluster degrees of freedom are built from center-of-mass boosted fragment wave functions and treated with resonating-group techniques. The norm kernel plays an important role: Pauli blocking suppresses cluster channels at small separations, restructures the relative-motion wave functions, and governs the normalization of clustering strength. As the central development we present a Green's function (GF) method that aids in resolving a long-standing difficulty of harmonic-oscillator based configuration interaction calculations that stems from wave functions with Gaussian asymptotics. The method restores the correct asymptotic behavior and extracts the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) with high accuracy even in very modest harmonic-oscillator spaces. The value of the ANC is very sensitive to the exact position of the state relative to threshold, and yet the GF method establishes the ANC as a structural observable that can be determined precisely from the interior wave function using the experimentally or otherwise known exact energy. A self-consistent iteration, formulated as an integral-operator eigenvalue problem, is also shown to recover both the energy and the ANC in cases when the energy of the state is to be determined. The method is illustrated for near-threshold states, such as the weakly bound $1^-$ state of $^{16}$O, as well as for the ground states of $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne.
papers.reason: Develops a Green's function method for configuration-interaction calculations of alpha clustering and asymptotic normalization coefficients, highly relevant to nuclear structure and low-energy nuclear responses.

papers.title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
papers.abstract: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. We derive the diquark interaction kernels arising from single instantons and instanton--anti-instanton molecules, revealing a strong attraction in the scalar channel and weaker correlations in the spin-one channels. Embedding these interactions in a covariant, permutation-symmetric Bethe--Salpeter--Faddeev equation yields a nucleon mass $m_N=939.53~{\rm MeV}$, with a predominantly scalar-diquark component ($98\%$) and a small axial-vector admixture ($2\%$) around the mass pole. Despite its small weight, the small admixture generates substantial spin--isospin interference, yielding an axial charge $g_A=1.265$, close to experiment. The resulting covariant amplitude is analytically continued to the light front to obtain the leading three-quark wave function. The corresponding unpolarized, helicity, and transversity parton distributions, along with their QCD-evolved moments, provide a direct connection to lattice QCD calculations and global-fit analyses. Our results show that the topology of the QCD vacuum organizes not only the nucleon mass and spin structure, but also its leading valence partonic content, providing a microscopic foundation for a more complete description including confinement and higher Fock components.
papers.reason: Derives nucleon mass, diquark correlation structure, axial charge, and light-front wave functions from the instanton liquid model of QCD vacuum topology, perfectly matching core nucleon structure interests.

papers.title: Effects of the $a_0(980)$ Meson on Finite Nuclei in a Parity Doublet Model
papers.abstract: We investigate nuclear structure within the parity doublet model (PDM), with particular emphasis on the role of the isovector-scalar $a_0(980)$ meson. We adopt the models with and without the $a_0$ meson and fit their parameters to nuclear matter saturation and ground state properties of selected nuclei, subject to constraints from the vacuum. The resulting parameter sets reproduce the nuclear matter saturation properties and provide a good description of binding energies and charge radii of selected nuclei. Our fits show that a large value of the chiral invariant mass of nucleon is preferred by the fitting: the best fitted value is $m_0 = 689 \pm 71 $ MeV with $a_0$ and $m_0 = 689 \pm 69 $ MeV without $a_0$. We find that the effects of the $a_0$ meson on the binding energies and charge radii are negligibly small. It is difficult to clarify the effect of $a_0$ meson to neutron skin thickness of Sn, Pb, and Ca isotopes, due to the large uncertainty of the predictions. We note that our prediction of $^{208} \text{Pb}$ is consistent with the measurement by PREX-II collaboration, while that of $^{48} \text{Ca}$ cannot explain the CREX result.
papers.reason: Examines finite nuclei structure and the role of the isovector-scalar a0(980) meson within a parity doublet model, directly relevant to chiral symmetry in nuclei and nuclear matter saturation.

papers.title: Glashow-Weinberg relation in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter
papers.abstract: The conservation of the axial-vector currents in nuclear matter with finite isospin asymmetry $\rho_n/\rho_p$ is explored in this paper. In explicit calculations in the in-medium chiral perturbation theory, a charged pion becomes massive in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter. In the presence of the massive charged pion, two components of the axial-vector current are not conserved from the two-loop order when applying the massive in-medium pion state. As a result, the in-medium Glashow-Weinberg relation for the charged pions cannot be derived in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter from operator relations in quantum chromodynamics.
papers.reason: Explores axial-vector current conservation and the in-medium Glashow-Weinberg relation for charged pions in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter using chiral perturbation theory, highly relevant to chiral EFT and nuclear electroweak processes.

papers.title: Scalar Non-standard Interactions in Type-II Seesaw
papers.abstract: We study the theoretical origin of scalar non-standard interactions (SNSI) in an \(A_4\)-symmetric Type-II seesaw model. The model contains an \(SU(2)_L\) scalar triplet \(\Delta\) and a real scalar singlet \(S\). After electroweak symmetry breaking, their CP-even neutral fluctuations mix to form two physical scalar states \(\phi_1\) and \(\phi_2\). These physical scalars couple to both neutrinos and charged leptons, establishing a connection between the neutrino sector and ordinary matter through scalar interactions. This induces a matter-dependent correction to the Type-II seesaw neutrino mass matrix. The SNSI contribution, governed by the relevant Yukawa couplings and the SNSI coefficient, can enhance or suppress the neutrino masses relative to their vacuum values. The model provides a simple and consistent description of how scalar mixing can give rise to SNSI and connects neutrino interactions in matter with the underlying structure of the scalar sector.
papers.reason: Studies the theoretical origin of scalar non-standard interactions (SNSI) in an A4-symmetric Type-II seesaw model linking neutrinos to matter, directly addressing core neutrino mass and NSI interests.

papers.title: Spontaneous CP violation and leptogenesis in minimal flavour models
papers.abstract: We consider a type-I seesaw framework extended by a scalar singlet whose vacuum expectation value (VEV) breaks CP spontaneously. The singlet VEV phase provides a common origin for low-energy leptonic CP violation and the high energy CP violation needed to generate the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) through leptogenesis. We identify two minimal flavour models based on a discrete $\mathcal{Z}_4$ symmetry, whose neutrino flavour structure is encoded entirely in the heavy Majorana mass matrix. Both models predict $\delta \simeq 3\pi/2$, a definite octant for the atmospheric $\theta_{23}$ mixing angle, and lower bounds of approximately $60~\mathrm{meV}$ ($50~\mathrm{meV}$) on the lightest neutrino mass and the effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$ for normal (inverted) ordering, within reach of future neutrinoless double-beta decay searches. We study scalar-singlet assisted leptogenesis in the non-resonant regime, including new decay, scattering, and washout processes involving the heavy scalars, as well as their contributions to the CP asymmetries. By solving the unflavoured Boltzmann equations, we identify the regions of parameter space in which the minimal flavour models successfully account for the observed BAU.
papers.reason: Examines spontaneous CP violation via a scalar singlet providing a common origin for leptonic CP violation and leptogenesis in minimal flavour models, hitting core neutrino mass, mixing, and leptogenesis interests.

papers.title: Inverse Problem Approach for Non-Perturbative QCD: Applications
papers.abstract: In arXiv:2211.13753 we proposed a novel theoretical approach for non-perturbative QCD, named the inverse problem approach. It extracts non-perturbative quantities by solving a dispersion integral equation as an inverse problem, using perturbative QCD and operator product expansion as inputs. In this work, we apply this approach to the pion and $a_1(1260)$ decay constants, as well as the continuum spectral function. The extracted $f_\pi = 130.8 \pm 8.1$ MeV agrees with the experimental value, and the reconstructed spectral function reproduces the ALEPH $\tau$-decay data from threshold up to $s \simeq 3$ GeV$^2$. The advantages of this approach are as follows: (i) the whole non-perturbative range is solved simultaneously, yielding the ground state, excited states, and the continuum spectrum within a single framework; (ii) it is based on rigorous mathematics, with not only statistical but also systematic uncertainties well controlled and quantifiable; (iii) the regularized solutions exhibit convergence, allowing the precision to be systematically improved with better inputs; (iv) quark-hadron duality emerges naturally at high energy scales, avoiding the low-energy duality assumption and the Borel transformation, and eliminating their associated uncertainties. Finally, the successful physical application of the inverse problem approach demonstrates its broad applicability to non-perturbative quantities.
papers.reason: Applies an inverse problem dispersion relation approach to extract non-perturbative QCD quantities (pion decay constant and spectral functions) from perturbative QCD and OPE, directly relevant to precision non-perturbative QCD methods.

papers.title: Comments on $\bf{\eta'}$ nuclei and on the $\Lambda$ binding energy of the hypertriton
papers.abstract: I briefly discuss two apparent puzzles: (i) is the observation of $\eta'$(958) bound states in $^{11}$C at GSI [1] compatible with a nearly vanishing real part of $\eta'N$ scattering length [2]? and (ii) is the $\Lambda$ binding energy of the hypertriton (${{_\Lambda}^3}$H), the lightest particle-stable hypernucleus, very small (63$^{+38}_{-31}$ keV, J-PARC E73 [3]) or very large (523$\pm$76 keV, MAMI [4])? Here, I suggest that MAMI's observed weak-decay pion momentum peak originates from ${{_\Lambda}^7}$He, not from ${{_\Lambda}^3}$H \cite{Gal26}.
papers.reason: Critically discusses eta-prime bound states in nuclei and resolves puzzles regarding the Lambda binding energy of the hypertriton, directly in core nuclear physics and hypernuclear interests.

papers.title: Off-lightcone Wilson-line operators in gradient flow at next-to-next-to-leading order
papers.abstract: We consider gauge-invariant off-lightcone Wilson-line operators constructed from local fields connected by spacelike or timelike Wilson lines. The lattice evaluation of their matrix elements requires a suitable renormalization prescription. Gradient flow offers such a prescription and, by smoothing the fields, suppresses ultraviolet fluctuations and can reduce statistical noise. We use the previously established matching framework based on the one-dimensional auxiliary-field formalism. In the small-flow-time limit, this framework reduces the matching of nonlocal off-lightcone Wilson-line operators to that of local current operators. We calculate the matching coefficients for these local current operators from the gradient-flow scheme to the modified minimal subtraction ($\MS$) scheme through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in QCD. Our results can be applied to lattice calculations of unpolarized and polarized quark and gluon quasi-parton distributions, as well as meson and baryon quasi-distribution amplitudes. They also apply to gluonic correlators entering quarkonium transport and heavy-quark momentum diffusion in the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). Further applications include quarkonium decay and production in potential nonrelativistic QCD (pNRQCD) and spin-dependent relativistic corrections to the static potential.
papers.reason: Calculates NNLO gradient-flow matching coefficients for off-lightcone Wilson-line operators relevant to quasi-parton distributions and heavy-quark diffusion, highly pertinent to lattice QCD inputs for neutrino and parton physics.

papers.title: Parity-violating M{\o}ller scattering: complete two-loop corrections
papers.abstract: The MOLLER experiment will measure the parity-violating asymmetry of M{\o}ller scattering to 2.4%. We present its fermionic and bosonic two-loop electroweak corrections to the zeroth and first orders in $1-4\sin^2\theta_W$. Light quarks enter through vacuum polarization from $e^+e^-$ data or lattice QCD. For $\sin^2\hat\theta_W(M_Z) = 0.23122$ and an 11 GeV beam, the weak charge of the electron is $0.04546(8)$ (data) or 0.04517(5) (lattice). Two-loop terms contribute 1.5% of it. Uncomputed terms are estimated at 4% of the experimental goal; the data-lattice difference, about 25% of that goal, limits the prediction.
papers.reason: Computes complete two-loop fermionic and bosonic electroweak corrections to parity-violating Moller scattering for the MOLLER experiment, squarely hitting high-precision electroweak physics and standard model radiative corrections.

papers.title: Enhanced Signal and Excited-State Control in Nonlocal Lattice Correlators
papers.abstract: Nonlocal correlation functions underpin lattice calculations of parton physics. However, their extraction is limited by a rapidly deteriorating signal-to-noise ratio with increasing Euclidean separation and hadron momentum, and by excited-state contamination. We propose a new fitting strategy that enhances control over both: by taking the ratio of nonlocal to local correlators, we can project out the dominant ground-state dynamics with a signal that is much cleaner and far less sensitive to excited states than the conventional approach. We demonstrate the method on the quark and gluon PDF, the quark GPD and TMDPDF. The results are consistent with those from the conventional three-point/two-point ratio fit but exhibit markedly improved precision and stability, and extend the accessible range to larger hadron momenta. For nonforward matrix elements such as GPDs, our strategy greatly simplifies the analysis procedure. Our method applies to general Dirac and momentum structures, for connected and disconnected contributions, and extends naturally to other nonlocal correlators, making it immediately deployable in existing lattice programs toward precision hadron structure.
papers.reason: Proposes a new fitting strategy using ratios of nonlocal to local correlators to drastically improve signal-to-noise and control excited states in lattice QCD calculations of PDFs, GPDs, and TMDPDFs—directly core to modern lattice inputs for neutrino-nucleus interactions.

papers.title: Glauber Description of Reaction Cross Sections with Bogoliubov Many-Body Wave Functions
papers.abstract: I developed a microscopic framework that connects relativistic nuclear density functional theory to high-energy reaction observables by incorporating many-body Bogoliubov wavefunctions, represented in Pfaffian form, into the Monte Carlo integration of the Glauber model. This approach enables a simultaneous treatment of nuclear pairing correlations and multiple-scattering effects beyond the optical limit approximation (OLA). The method is applied to reaction cross sections of even-even O, Ne, and Mg isotopes on a $^{12}$C target. Complete multiple-scattering calculations systematically reduce the cross sections relative to the OLA and improves the agreement with measured interaction cross sections. Applications to the deformed Ne and Mg isotopes show that calculations based on a single intrinsic orientation depend strongly on the angle between the nuclear symmetry axis and the beam direction. Angular-momentum projection removes the spurious dependence on the arbitrarily selected intrinsic orientation and produces smooth isotopic systematics for the laboratory-frame cross sections. This work establishes a microscopic bridge between relativistic nuclear structure theory and reaction dynamics, providing a general framework for exploring exotic phenomena such as halos and clustering.
papers.reason: Connects relativistic nuclear density functional theory to reaction cross sections using Bogoliubov wavefunctions in the Glauber model, perfectly matching nuclear structure inputs for scattering.

papers.title: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays
papers.abstract: We propose a new method to search for fifth forces at micron scales, by resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms in optical tweezer arrays. We develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry, which can approach the Standard Quantum Limit, and expand the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints. We show that this level of sensitivity can also probe well-motivated models of extra dimensions beyond the current tabletop state of the art, by leveraging the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.
papers.reason: Proposes cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays to search for micron-range fifth forces, directly tied to precision atomic/nuclear probes of new physics.

papers.title: Precision Studies of Boosted Polarized Vector Bosons with Energy Correlators
papers.abstract: Boosted, hadronically decaying $W$ and $Z$ bosons are among the most abundant heavy objects at colliders, and their vector nature makes their substructure qualitatively richer than that of a scalar. We initiate precision studies of the hadronic decays of boosted polarized vector bosons with energy correlators. In the narrow-width limit, the laboratory-frame two-point energy correlator is a sum of longitudinal and transverse decay spectra, each weighted by its polarized production rate and obtained by a closed-form boost kernel acting on rest-frame correlators. Combining polarized production density matrices, computed at NNLO in QCD for $pp\to V+X$ and at leading order for $e^+e^-\to W^+W^-$, with decay correlators that combine NNLO fixed order with NNLL collinear and N$^4$LL back-to-back resummation, we find for high-$p_T$ $W/Z$ production that polarization shifts the spectrum by $\mathcal{O}(10\%)$ relative to a naive unpolarized treatment. Even without any reconstruction, hadronic $W/Z$ decays stand out over the realistic QCD background of untagged jet samples as a localized angular bump. Our results open the door to using energy correlators for polarimetry of electroweak bosons through their hadronic decays, for standard-candle measurements of electroweak bosons inside jets, and in sharper searches for new resonances.
papers.reason: Uses energy correlators for precision studies of boosted polarized W/Z bosons, highly relevant to high-energy electroweak boson substructure and standard candles.

papers.title: An Eigenvector-Continued Green's Function Method
papers.abstract: Emulating the Green's function using reduced-order equations is challenging because of the amount of information it contains. This information includes the one-particle spectroscopy over the entire energy spectrum, the one-body density matrix, and the ground-state energy. Nevertheless, the computational speedup offered by emulators is essential for applications requiring repeated model evaluations, which are ubiquitous in many-body physics. These include parameter calibration, uncertainty quantification, phase-diagram mapping, and geometry optimization. In this Letter, we introduce a systematically improvable emulator based on eigenvector continuation and moment-matching. The resulting approximation, which we refer to as an ``eigenvector-continued Green's function,'' can be obtained by solving linear equations, enabling an efficient separation of the computational workload into offline and online stages.
papers.reason: Introduces an ab initio reduced-order emulator for many-body Green's functions based on eigenvector continuation and moment matching, highly relevant to nuclear many-body calculations.

papers.title: Proton GTMDs and Wigner Distributions in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model: Orbital Angular Momentum and Spin-Orbit Correlation with Sea Quarks
papers.abstract: We calculate the leading-twist vector and axial-vector quark generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) of the proton in the chiral quark soliton model, including both the discrete valence level and the regularized Dirac sea. We consider the isosinglet and isotriplet combinations of GTMDs at zero and nonzero skewness. At zero skewness, we construct Wigner distributions and resolve the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit correlation (SOC) densities in transverse position and momentum space, separately for quarks and antiquarks. This provides a phase-space picture of the sea-quark and sea-antiquark contributions, displaying OAM aligned with the proton spin and anti-aligned with the partons' own spin.
papers.reason: Calculates vector and axial-vector quark GTMDs and Wigner distributions in the chiral quark soliton model, directly relevant to nucleon spin structure and parton distributions.

papers.title: A doubly charmed strange molecule from coupled-channel dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate a doubly charmed molecular state $T_{cc\bar{s}}$ with $C=+2$, $\mathcal{S}=+1$, and $I=1/2$ in an off-shell coupled-channel formalism. Constructing the interaction kernel from a meson-exchange model based on an effective Lagrangian and solving the coupled-channel scattering equation in the Blankenbecler-Sugar reduction, we find a pole only for $J^P=1^+$ among $J^P=0^\pm$, $1^\pm$, and $2^\pm$. With the reduced cutoff mass of $600$~MeV, we obtain a mass of $3972.90$~MeV, which corresponds to a binding energy of $4.01$~MeV relative to the $D^*D_s$ threshold. Examining the relative signs and magnitudes of the $S$-wave channel couplings extracted from the pole residues, we demonstrate that the pole belongs predominantly to the triplet ($\mathbf{3}_A$) representation. We also discuss the relevance of heavy-quark spin symmetry to the bound state.
papers.reason: Investigates the doubly charmed molecular state Tccbar(s) using an off-shell coupled-channel meson-exchange model, directly relevant to hadronic molecular dynamics and few-body nuclear systems.

papers.title: Enhanced structure-dependent alpha decay tunneling in deformed odd-odd nuclei via intense two-color laser pulses
papers.abstract: In the present work, we investigate the effect of ultra-intense laser fields on the $\alpha$ decay tunneling of deformed odd-odd nuclei. Calculations performed within the deformed density-dependent cluster model show that, for deformed odd-odd $\alpha$ emitters, the laser-induced variation in the penetration probability separates into distinct branches associated with different valence particle-hole configurations relative to the $Z=82$ and $N=126$ shell closures. In contrast to the even-even and odd-$A$ cases, the odd-odd parent nucleus most sensitive to the laser field is not the one with the lowest $\alpha$ decay energy. This indicates that the laser response is governed not only by $Q_{\alpha}$ but also by structural correlations associated with the simultaneously unpaired proton and neutron. We further examine the pulse-averaged response under a two-color laser field. The results show that an optimized two-color field enhances the pulse-averaged laser response for most of the studied nuclei, while highly sensitive nuclei exhibit an effective gain equivalent to increasing the laser intensity by more than one order of magnitude. These findings identify structural determinants of laser-assisted $\alpha$ decay in odd-odd nuclei and provide guidance for selecting candidate nuclei and optimizing laser parameters in future experiments.
papers.reason: Studies alpha decay tunneling in deformed odd-odd nuclei under intense laser pulses using a density-dependent cluster model, connecting closely to low-energy nuclear structure and decay dynamics.

papers.title: Finite-Size Heavy-Diquarks and State-Dependent Corrections to Heavy Antiquark-Diquark Symmetry
papers.abstract: Heavy antiquark-diquark symmetry (HADS) maps a compact color-antitriplet heavy pair onto a pointlike antiquark source, but retaining a finite diquark mass does not retain its spatial extent. We develop a finite-size framework that treats the heavy diquark as a composite cluster with an independently determined mass and scale. A unified peak-height-weighted radius prescription applies to ground and radially excited diquarks in nonstrange and strange environments. For 16 selected states of $\Xi_{cc}$, $\Omega_{cc}$, $\Xi_{bb}$, and $\Omega_{bb}$, the mean absolute mass deviation from the central AL1 three-body spectrum falls from 108 MeV in the point-source limit to 10 MeV, without fitting to baryon levels. The structure-resolution angle defines $\delta_{\rm HADS}=1-\langle\cos\hat\theta\rangle$, a quantitative, state-dependent measure of the finite-size contribution to HADS breaking. Internal excitation increases this correction, whereas external excitation reduces it, demonstrating that the same heavy source can be resolved differently by distinct surrounding states. Comparisons across reference potentials preserve these trends and the spectral improvement.
papers.reason: Develops a finite-size framework for heavy diquarks and state-dependent corrections to heavy antiquark-diquark symmetry in doubly heavy baryons, very relevant to modern hadron structure methods.

papers.title: Searching for axion-like particles with space-based optical lattice clock networks
papers.abstract: Axion like particles (ALPs) are particularly well motivated candidates for dark matter, and physics beyond the Standard Model more generally. However, direct detection remains extremely challenging due to the weakness of their interactions. In this work, we propose to employ space-based optical lattice clock networks (SOLCN), originally targeted to probe the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB), to detect axion dark matter through cosmic birefringence via minor modifications to their laser links. Searching for cross-correlated signals then provides significant sensitivity to low mass ALPs as a result of their large correlation lengths. In this work we focus on ALPs in the mass range $10^{-18.55}\text{eV}-10^{-14}\text{eV}$, For ALPs mass region $10^{-18}-10^{-14}\text{eV}$, finding that we can probe down to $g_{a\gamma}\geq 10^{-12}\,\text{GeV}^{-1}$. Moreover, we find that the SOLCN sensitivity to the ALP-photon coupling depends crucially on the frequency of the network link. With an $8$ GHz frequency link, we then have the potential to reach $g_{a\gamma}\geq10^{-16}\,\text{GeV}^{-1}$ in this region.
papers.reason: Proposes space-based optical lattice clock networks to detect axion dark matter through cosmic birefringence, aligning well with precision atomic probes of new physics.

papers.title: From Colour--Casimir Recoupling to Near-Threshold Scattering: Algebraic Diagnostics and a Pion-Mass Test for the $T_{cc}^{+}$ Channel
papers.abstract: The near-threshold $T_{cc}^{+}$ is a clean testing ground for how constituent-level colour structure connects to hadronic scattering. We report three results and state what each does and does not establish. (i)~\emph{Colour algebra.} In the two-dimensional colour-singlet basis of $cc\bar u\bar d$, a general pairwise colour operator has direct $DD^*$ matrix element $V_{MM}=-\tfrac43(v_{13}+v_{24})$, containing only the two intra-meson coefficients, while meson--hidden-colour mixing is $V_{MH}^{\rm off}=\tfrac{\sqrt2}{3}\Delta_v$ with $\Delta_v=v_{14}+v_{23}-v_{12}-v_{34}$; uniform edges give no mixing. The projection is exact within this basis and is checked numerically on 10\,000 random edge assignments. A same-Hamiltonian decomposition shows that it re-expresses the central colour operator ($116.46$ MeV off-diagonal) rather than adding an independent dynamical input. (ii)~\emph{Negative dynamical results.} For Coulomb-type Gaussian edges the hidden-colour diagonal lies below the meson diagonal, so the attractive second-order shift $-2\Delta_v^2/(9\Delta_H)$ does not apply. In a Gaussian constituent Hamiltonian calibrated to $M_D$ and $M_{D^*}$, the lowest compact level lies $148.6$ MeV above its model $DD^*$ threshold (iii)~\emph{Pion-mass test.} Couplings fixed at the $m_\pi\simeq280$ MeV lattice pole ($-5.2$ MeV) are carried to $m_\pi\simeq391$ MeV by changing only the reduced mass and compact-sector gap, both refitted to the lattice $D$ and $D^*$ masses. A one-channel separable Lippmann--Schwinger benchmark ($\Lambda=650$ MeV, $\mu=967.7$ MeV, $C_G\simeq-36.15~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$) is calibrated to the $5.2$ MeV pole and serves only as a regulator-sensitivity study. We do not reproduce the complex lattice pole or perform a full coupled-channel calculation.
papers.reason: Analyzes color-Casimir recoupling, hidden-color mixing, and pion-mass tests for the near-threshold Tcc+ channel, directly in line with hadronic molecular dynamics and lattice-QCD comparisons.

papers.title: Majorana Neutrino Physics and Matter-Antimatter Asymmetry in Type IIA String Theory
papers.abstract: We study Majorana neutrino masses and the matter-antimatter asymmetry in Type IIA string theory on a $T^6/(\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2)$ orientifold with intersecting D6-branes. Euclidean D2-instantons with $\text{Sp}(2)$ Chan-Paton symmetry generate both the seesaw mechanism and the Weinberg operator. The flavour vectors are not computed from a compactification but fixed by matching, so our results are an existence proof. Matching the measured mass-squared differences selects the seesaw-dominated case with normal ordering. Swampland criteria constrain the instanton action and the reheating temperature. A benchmark example reproduces the neutrino parameters, gives $\eta_B \approx 8.6 \times 10^{-11}$, within an order of magnitude of observation, and predicts $\langle m_{\beta \beta} \rangle =2.594 \text{meV}$. A parameter scan shows the mass hierarchy is accommodated rather than predicted.
papers.reason: Studies Majorana neutrino masses, the seesaw mechanism, and matter-antimatter asymmetry via Euclidean D2-instantons in Type IIA string theory with orientifolds, connecting string-theoretic realizations to low-energy neutrino parameters.

papers.title: Deposition of $\alpha$ clusters on the surface of $^{28}$Si
papers.abstract: The possibility of the appearance of the clustering structure in the surface is one of the key features determining the nuclear structural properties. In this work, we study the ground-state structure of $^{28}\text{Si}$ using the antisymmetrized quasicluster model (AQCM), focusing on the deposition of the $\alpha$ cluster structure on the surface. Three candidate structural configurations constrained to reproduce the experimental charge radius are investigated based on the $\text{SU}(3)$ shell model, the $j$-$j$ coupling shell model, and a localized $7\alpha$ cluster model. Using Glauber-model calculations for intermediate-energy proton elastic scattering, we demonstrate that the angular distribution at and beyond the first diffraction peak is highly sensitive to surface diffuseness, and that the $7\alpha$ cluster model configuration best reproduces the experimental data due to its sharper surface profile. Also, the elastic charge form factors from electron scattering support the existence of the cluster-induced oblately deformed structure.
papers.reason: Studies the ground-state structure and surface alpha-clustering of Si-28 using AQCM and Glauber-model proton scattering, very relevant to nuclear structure and cluster models.

papers.title: The $K T_{cc}(3875)$ Interaction: Bound State, Scattering Observables and Correlation Function
papers.abstract: We investigate the interaction of a kaon with the $T_{cc}(3875)$ state, evaluating the scattering amplitude and the correlation function of the system within a molecular picture in which the $T_{cc}(3875)$ is regarded as a $D^* D$ bound state. Since the $KD^*$ and $KD$ interactions dynamically generate the $D_{s1}(2460)$ and $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ resonances, respectively, both of which are significantly bound with respect to their corresponding particle thresholds, the $KT_{cc}(3875)$ interaction is found to be strongly attractive, leading to the formation of two bound states with binding energies of about 63 MeV and 51 MeV, respectively, with respect to the $KT_{cc}(3875)$ threshold. We also determine the scattering observables at threshold, including the scattering length and effective range, and calculate the correlation function. The latter exhibits features similar to those found in previous studies of the scattering of an external particle off a dynamically generated resonance of molecular nature.
papers.reason: Investigates the kaon-Tcc(3875) interaction and scattering observables using a molecular picture where Tcc is a D*D bound state, highly relevant to hadronic molecules and coupled-channel dynamics.

papers.title: Heavy-Particle Effective Theory: from On-Shell Formalism to Gravitational Compton Amplitudes
papers.abstract: We formulate on-shell heavy-particle effective theory (HPET) amplitudes by projecting the spinor-helicity variables onto the $SU(2)$ little group of a timelike reference velocity $v^{\mu}$. Retaining both large and small components of the velocity-projected spinors gives an intermediate velocity-projected amplitudes in which reparameterization invariance can be imposed before expanding in the inverse heavy-particle mass. Integrating out the small component then yields HPET amplitudes organized by heavy-particle power counting, with a direct correspondence to local operators at fixed order. We determine the three-point velocity-projected amplitudes for two equal-mass particles of arbitrary spin $S$ coupled to a soft massless boson of helicity $h$. Four-point gravitational Compton amplitudes can be constructively obtained using velocity-projected three-point amplitudes, and expanded into HPET amplitudes which is free of spurious poles up to sub-leading order. As a gravitational application, we show that the projected gravitational minimal coupling reproduces the Kerr spin-induced multipoles up to order $2S$, and find the classical limits of the tree-level elastic gravitational scattering and gravitational Compton amplitudes agreed with the literature up to contact terms undetermined by factorization.
papers.reason: Formulates on-shell heavy-particle effective theory (HPET) amplitudes and derives gravitational Compton amplitudes and spin-induced multipoles, directly relevant to modern EFT and gravitational scattering methods.

papers.title: FCC-\mu e: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN
papers.abstract: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $\mu^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including the exciting prospect of measurements of the Higgs boson self-interaction, and is followed by a presentation of the FCC-$\mu e$ layout -- from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$\mu e$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.
papers.reason: Proposes a high-energy muon-electron collider and associated neutrino factory at CERN, directly tying into future neutrino experimental facilities.

papers.title: Neutron Optical Constraints on Exotic Parity-odd Interactions between Neutrons and Nucleons
papers.abstract: Many theories beyond the standard model of particle physics predict the existence of weakly-coupled exotic spin-dependent interactions between standard model particles. We use experimental upper bounds on neutron-nucleus parity violation at meV and keV neutron energies in the forward scattering limit described by neutron optics to constrain exotic parity-odd interactions of the neutron with nucleons from exotic vector boson exchange for force ranges between $10^{-2}$ to $10^{-14}$ meters.
papers.reason: Uses neutron-nucleus parity violation data and neutron optics to constrain exotic parity-odd interactions and vector boson exchanges, perfectly aligning with low-energy precision probes of BSM physics.

papers.title: Orientation effects of deformed nuclei in intermediate-energy nuclear scattering
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of nuclear deformation on intermediate-energy nuclear scattering within the Glauber theory. A formalism that explicitly incorporates the orientation dependence of deformed intrinsic states is derived, in which reaction observables are first computed with a fixed orientation and then the angle average of the reaction observables is taken afterwards. This formalism is applied to elastic scattering and total reaction cross sections. In addition, a new expansion scheme of the optical-limit approximation is proposed and shown to include contributions from a class of nuclear excitations, allowing a simple estimate of part of the total inelastic scattering cross section. The orientation dependence is generally weak for both proton- and carbon-target scattering and supports the validity of conventional treatments with an angle averaged density for light and medium-heavy nuclei. However, noticeable deviations emerge for strongly deformed heavy nuclei. The present analysis further demonstrates that the summed inelastic scattering cross section to rotationally excited states can be interpreted as a manifestation of fluctuations of the nuclear surface density associated with deformation.
